request.state: Evaluate an attachment boundary for Can, an adoption-oriented SaaS DSL whose only current products are source specifications and handwritten desired JavaScript. Neither compiling code, shared file handling nor a chatbot host adapter exists yet. Reducing repeated source must preserve mandatory business evidence. The existing §8 contract requires permission before upload, receipt of actual bytes under quota and type/size rules, immutable completion, and removal of abandoned objects. A completed file reference is opaque. New uploads belong to the selected app, team and authenticated principal; reusing an existing attachment requires its readable owning record/field. Bare identifiers authorize nothing. The §10 browser/MCP surface is generated from one operation registry, authenticates a fixed app/user/team connection, revalidates live permissions and uses operation_id for mutations. The real CanExpense Expense.create signature contains mandatory receipt:file. Its finalized-file fixtures are test setup, not production provision. Checked MCP 2025-11-25 allows vendor _meta entries; resources/read returns resources from a server rather than uploading a user's file. There is no demonstrated universal chatbot upload support. A user-selected file may be available to a Can-aware host, or the host may lack that integration entirely. All alternatives must preserve equal attachment rights, destination bounds, quota/content validation and final operation admission. Prohibit substituting local paths, URLs or file-property objects for content; model-controlled transfer destinations/storage keys; repeated app upload definitions; and claims of tested operation. Judge the furnished context, not speculative runtime timings or external research.

handoff.instructions: Recommend the minimum sufficient attachment contract, considering genuine client limitations, source economy, reuse, workflow friction and the amount of data passed through model calls.

criteria.shared_host_flow: A generated _meta descriptor identifies a versioned Can upload bridge. A host implementing it sends the selected bytes through the already-defined browser HTTPS authorization/upload/finalization service, returning its file ID to the ordinary operation arguments. Field/record associations come from the canonical registry, with no independently authored upload definition. If the host cannot use this bridge, present a truthful browser-based transfer path. Bytes need not enter model context and both surfaces share machinery, but there is a real adapter/extension implementation burden and generic MCP hosts remain unsupported for in-chat transfer.
criteria.runtime_tools: Make infrastructure-level upload-start, base64-chunk and upload-finish tools available on the MCP server, using the same owner, input and permission constraints. The resulting ID is consumed by the normal business tool; source apps add no custom upload scenario. This uses tool transport for content and avoids an additional HTTP bridge specification. It still depends on host access to the user's bytes and robust chunk handling, and encoded tool payloads can substantially enlarge model context; tool protocol availability alone cannot grant local-file access.
criteria.browser_only: Specify no new chatbot byte-transfer facility: the user always uploads new content using the generated browser interface and then passes that completed, authorized reference through MCP. This leaves validation shared and avoids both extension maintenance and content-transfer tools. It also imposes an external browser step on file-capable hosts and leaves fresh attachments unavailable as a wholly conversational workflow.
